text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 7142 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.

- The cabinet moved to facilitate the creation of a second telecommuncations network to compete with Matav by allowing thestate railways MAV to transfer its telephone lines running along railway tracks to other business partnerships.
- The election of party officials and a strategy for the 1998 elections will be the two biggest issues facing this weekend's Socialist Party conference in Budapest.

- The Young Democrats will release an Opposition Declaration on June 12 that party president Viktor Orban said could become a basic document for a change of government in 1998, and could serve as a rallying point for opposition unity.
- Parliament extended the mandate of the social insurance authorities by 60 days.
- The state privatisation agency APV 1997 revenues wil probably exceed the projected 180 billion forints, CEO Pal Szabo told reporters.

- The managing director, environmental proction director and plant supervisor of Grabo Kft, a subsidiary of Graboplast Rt, have been charged with illegal disposal of environmentally harmful material. Grabo management says the waste is not dangerous to the environment and they are of the opinion that the entire affair is an attempt to injure Grabo's reputation.
- The US will probably withdraw Hungary's GSP treatment in the next two of three years, Washington trade councilor Ferenc Furulyas told the newspaper.
- A draft agruculture bill will be made public in two weeks, Agriculture Ministry state secretary Zoltan Kis told the sector's representatives in Nyiregyhaza.
